correctness.rationale: The weak B2 definition uses sums of **distinct unordered pairs**, not repeated-index Sidon sums. At modulus 56, translating any 9-set to contain zero is valid. The independent ascending recursive checker enumerates every 0=a0<a1<...<a8<56, branching exactly when new pair sums x+a_i avoid all prior and among themselves; no prunable prefix could lead to a valid full set if collision exists, and cardinality pruning is exact. It traversed 3,455,863 nodes and found precisely 216 valid zero-containing sets. A separate affine-orbit enumerator forms uS0+t for all 24 units u and 56 translations t, found 1344 distinct sets, exactly 216 containing zero, and compared each normalized set with the census. This proves one full affine orbit, free group action and count 1344. Every asserted classification concerns only finite Z56; this finite exhaustion is the actual complete proof, not sampling.
correctness.risk: This is not a uniqueness theorem for all composite-DNA codes or for all moduli and set sizes; it proves only weak distinct-pair sums at (k,q)=(9,56).

An important newly located Haanpää–Östergård research report (2004) and JNT article (2007) compute exact Abelian-group extremal quantities using backtracking with isomorph rejection over groups up to order 183, including possibly Z56; they are **plausibly covering** but their full PDFs were unavailable. The abstracts describe maximum sizes and v(k), not an explicit theorem enumerating the 1344 cyclic Z56 solutions or single free orbit.
